title: Structure template-transplant lever feasibility (read-only assessment)
context: Cycle 285 identified rigid-align ligand transplant from the 64 holo crystals as the only no-GPU structure lever. This assesses whether a close-enough crystal exists to make it worth building.
method: ECFP4 (Morgan radius 2, 2048 bit) on standardized SMILES; per-test-ligand max Tanimoto over the 56 unique holo ligands. Independently reproduces scripts/nb361_pdb64_inventory.py.
interpretation: The 64 holo crystals are drug-like PXR agonists (MW 400-700, complex multi-ring scaffolds, e.g. 8R81/Y8B benzimidazole MW 405). The 184 structure-test ligands are small fragment-like molecules (e.g. NS(=O)(=O)C=1C=CC=2CCCC2C1). Scaffold mismatch is total: the single best test-to-holo pair across all 184x56 comparisons reaches only Tanimoto 0.317, well below the 0.5 transplant gate. Rigid-align ligand transplant requires a near-isosteric crystal analog (typically sim>=0.7 for a defensible pose) to place atoms meaningfully; here the maximum-common-substructure overlap is far too small for the transplanted coordinates to map onto the test ligand.
recommendation: Do NOT build the template-transplant lever. Coverage at sim>=0.5 is 0 (need >30); even the loosest reasonable gate (sim>=0.4) yields 0 ligands. The holo set and the test set occupy disjoint chemical space (drug-like agonists vs small fragments). Given the documented history that every post-hoc structure pose-swap has HURT LDDT-PLI under strict gating (v4 -0.0049, v6 -0.0364), and that 0 ligands would even pass the gate, this lever cannot produce a single transplant and carries only downside risk. Structure track should remain on the pure multi-seed Boltz-2 v5 safety floor (LDDT-PLI 0.4996, rank 10/50). The only paths that could move the structure track are GPU-bound (Boltz-2 re-runs), consistent with cycle-285's no-GPU-lever conclusion.
gate_summary: coverage(sim>=0.5)=0 of 184; coverage(sim>=0.7)=0 of 184; max observed sim=0.317; NO-GO.
